turns.t: Good afternoon, doctor. I'm a bit worried because my shoulders have been very stiff and sore, and a friend said it might be polymyalgia.
Thank you for coming. Tell me about the shoulders. When do they feel worst?
In the morning. I can hardly lift my arms to wash my hair. It takes about an hour to loosen up.
Is it both shoulders?
Both. And my hips, a little, too.
How long has this been going on?
About five weeks.
Any fever, weight loss, or headaches over your temples?
No fever. No weight loss. No headaches.
Any pain when you chew, or changes in your vision?
No, nothing like that. My jaw is fine.
Have you had any joint swelling, or rashes?
No swelling, and my skin is fine.
Let me take your pulse, blood pressure, temperature and oxygen level. ~
Of course.
Pulse 72, blood pressure 130 over 78, temperature 36.7, oxygen 98 percent, breathing 15.
Everything's normal? ~
Normal. I'd like to move your shoulders and check the strength. ~
Go ahead.
You have a good range of movement but it's painful at the extremes, and your strength is normal.
So what do you think it is? ~
The pattern fits polymyalgia rheumatica, but I can't be certain until the blood tests are back.
What blood tests?
Inflammatory markers, a full blood count, and a check of your kidneys and thyroid.
And if they're high? ~
Then we'd talk about a short steroid course, which usually works very quickly. ~
Is there anyone in the family I should be concerned about? ~
Does anyone in your family have rheumatic or autoimmune conditions?
My mother had rheumatoid arthritis.
Thank you, that's useful. Do you smoke or drink?
I gave up smoking ten years ago. And I drink very little.
Good. I'll phone you as soon as the results are in. ~
Thank you. ~
If you get a new headache, jaw pain or changes to your vision, call us the same day.
I will. ~
